commitResults.messageTitle: Add undo command to restore deleted persons
commitResults.messageBody:
A deleted person cannot be recovered, as the address book is saved to
disk after every command.

Let's add an `undo` command that restores the most recently deleted
person, as described in UC4 of the Developer Guide. Keep the deletion
history of the current session in ModelManager.

Reject arguments, as `undo 2` is ambiguous. Refuse to restore a person
who already exists, leaving them on top of the deletion history so undo
can retry once the clash is resolved. Also mention undo in the delete
success message.

The undo command and the deletion history in ModelManager have no tests.

Let's add tests for restoring deletions most recent first, including
from a filtered list, and for the failure cases: nothing to undo, a
person who already exists, and arguments given to undo. Also test that
ModelManager records, restores and compares deletion history.

The User Guide does not mention undo, so users cannot find out that a
deletion can be reversed.

Let's document what undo restores and its limits: it reverts only
delete, lasts for the current session, adds the person to the end of the
list, fails if the same person exists, and takes no parameters.
Add Codecov badge

commitResults.messageTitle: Document case-insensitive command words in User Guide
Switch field prefixes to Unix-style flags
commitResults.messageBody:
The add and edit commands use AB3-style prefixes (n/, p/, ...), while
newer commands such as sort and depart already use Unix-style options.

Replace the prefixes with short and long flags: -n/--name, -p/--phone,
-e/--email, -a/--address and -t/--tag.

Prefix now holds aliases, and equality uses the primary form only. Both
forms therefore share one ArgumentMultimap key, and `-e a --email b` is
reported as a repeated field.

ArgumentTokenizer matches every form of a prefix, and only when it is
a separate word. A value such as `Blk 5 -apt 3` is not split, and
`-nJohn` is not read as a flag.

Test helpers glued values to prefixes (n/Amy), which the tokenizer no
longer accepts once prefixes must be separate words.

Insert a space after each flag in CommandTestUtil and PersonUtil.

Add tests for long-form aliases, mixing short and long forms, repeated
flags in either form, values glued to a flag, and clearing tags with
--tag.

The user guide and developer guide still show the old n/-style
prefixes.

Replace every example with the new flags, list the short and long
forms, and explain that a flag must be a separate word.
Synchronise use case syntax

commitResults.messageTitle: Unify add and edit flag parsing in one tokenizer
commitResults.messageBody:
add used AddArgumentTokenizer for long options and ArgumentTokenizer
for short flags, so add and edit followed different rules for mixing
flags, quotes and tags.

Move add's features into ArgumentTokenizer and use it for add, edit
and depart:
- Short and long flags can be mixed in one command.
- A quoted word is literal text, so a value can contain a flag, e.g.
  -a "Blk 5 -t 3". Quotes inside a word are ordinary characters.
- Each word after -t/--tag is a separate tag.
- Unknown -- options and unmatched quotes are rejected.

Duplicate-field errors now name both forms of a flag, e.g. -e/--email.

Remove AddArgumentTokenizer, which is no longer used.

commitResults.messageTitle: Apply add's phone and tag validation to edit
commitResults.messageBody:
AddCommandParser checks that phones have 7-15 digits and strips a
leading '#' or '/' from tags itself, before calling ParserUtil.
EditCommandParser calls ParserUtil directly, so it skips both rules:
`edit 1 -p 123` and 25-digit phones are accepted, while
`edit 1 -t #friend` is rejected although `add` accepts it.

Let's move both rules, and their error messages, from
AddCommandParser and AddCommand into ParserUtil#parsePhone and
ParserUtil#parseTag, so that add and edit apply the same rules to
user input.

Phone#isValidPhone still accepts 3 or more digits, so data files
with shorter numbers saved by earlier versions still load.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update parser tests for shared phone and tag rules
commitResults.messageBody:
ParserUtil enforces add's 7-15 digit phone rule and strips a leading
'#' or '/' from tags, and the related error messages have moved from
AddCommand to ParserUtil. Several tests still refer to the removed
constants or rely on the old, looser rules: ParserUtilTest treats a
6-digit phone as valid and "#friend" as an invalid tag, and
EditCommandParserTest expects edit's old phone error message.

Let's point those tests at the new constants and replace the
outdated example values.

Also add tests for the edit inputs that used to slip through, such
as `edit 1 -p 123` and `edit 1 -t #friend`, together with the 7- and
15-digit boundaries and the 30-character tag limit. A later change
that makes add and edit diverge again then fails a test.

Let's describe the rules as applying to both commands, and explain

commands stay consistent.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Document how undo restores deleted contacts
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG's undo section describes AB3's proposed undo/redo design,
which saves a copy of the whole address book after every change.
The app does not use that design. Its undo reverses only delete,
using a stack of deleted persons kept in ModelManager, and there is
no redo. Developers reading the DG would look for classes and
methods that do not exist, such as VersionedAddressBook.

Let's replace that section with a description of the actual
implementation, and add a sequence diagram of undo through Logic
and Model, modelled on the existing delete diagram.

The section also records the two main design decisions, storing
only the deleted person and keeping the history in ModelManager,
with the alternatives considered.

commitResults.messageTitle: Redesign GUI as dashboard with detail popups
commitResults.messageBody:
The main window stacks a mouse-oriented menu bar, a command box, a
fixed-height result box and tall contact cards. Only about five
contacts fit, errors lose their examples to the cut-off result box,
and one details window covers the list and shows a single contact.

Our target user types fast, prefers the keyboard and manages many
contacts, so the window should read like a terminal tool.

Let's lay the window out as numbered panes:

* [1] Departments: counts for all contacts, contacts with no
  department, and each department
* [2] Contacts: one compact row per contact under a header row
* [4] Output: feedback that grows to fit errors, above a prompt
* footer: key hints, shown and total counts, data file path

Contact details become [3]: one popup per viewed contact, showing
the fields as a grid of copyable values, so several contacts can be
compared side by side. Viewing a contact again refreshes its popup
instead of opening another, and the prompt keeps the focus.

Add keyboard navigation: Alt+1 to Alt+4 and Esc move between panes,
j/k move within lists, Enter or a double-click on a row views that
contact, and q closes a popup. The menu bar is hidden but kept, as
its Help item provides the F1 shortcut.

CommandResult carries the viewed Person, which the UI uses to find
the popup already showing that contact. Logic exposes the unfiltered
person and department lists for the sidebar and footer. view groups
how to reach a contact above department and tags, without a header.

The help window and popups share the dashboard theme. The font stays
AB3's Segoe UI, which falls back to the system font on macOS and
Linux.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add docked details pane beside contact list
commitResults.messageBody:
Contact details appear only in popups, which view, Enter or a
double-click on a row opens. Each popup is a new OS window, so
glancing through contacts feels slow: Windows creates the window,
plays its open animation, and moves the focus there and back.

Let's dock a [3] Details pane beside the contact list:

* the pane shows the contact selected with a click or j/k at once,
  without running a command
* view, Enter and double-click still open one popup per contact for
  side-by-side comparison
* repeated Alt+3 steps through the pane, then each popup, then back
  to the pane
* the pane shows a hint until a contact is selected

ViewCommand.formatDetails is public, so the pane shows a contact
exactly as view does. The contact table's columns are narrower, to
make room for the pane.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show every wrapped line of long detail values
commitResults.messageBody:
Values in the details pane and popups stay one line tall, so a long
address can only be read by scrolling inside its field. The binding
that fits each value's height to its text is never set up, as it
looks up the text before the value's own scroll pane is skinned.

Let's look up the text through the scroll pane's content, which
already holds it, so each value grows to show every wrapped line.

A DetailsPanelTest case checks that a long address wraps and stays
fully visible.
